# X player card for a game ## Voyager publishing Use [publish-game](../../publish-game/SKILL.md) for a requested public release. Voyager is the default host, using the existing account and a permanent `https://-.voyager.site` root URL. Cloudflare Pages below is an alternative only when the user chooses their own hosting. Choose a short readable game slug on first publication with `--slug moon-hop`; avoid brand names or misleading affiliation. The server adds its six-character suffix. Use the returned URL, such as `https://moon-hop-a2b3c4.voyager.site`, rather than deriving a hostname from the game's internal ID. Updates and title changes preserve this URL; changing `--slug` after creation produces a warning and keeps the original link. An X release **requires a square PNG/JPEG/WebP poster with the title and "Tap to play"**. Aim for 1200×1200 with text readable at card size. Include it in the built folder, then pass `--thumbnail-path poster.png` to both prepare and publish. Studio supplies `twitter:card=player`, the stable root plus `?embed=1` as `twitter:player`, and width/height `480`. It escapes the title, versions the poster URL, and supplies headers permitting any site to frame the game. Inspect the emitted `twitter:image` instead of guessing its storage path. The upload manifest still contains only `schema_version`, `entrypoint`, optional `thumbnail_path` and `files`. Do not add player URL or dimension fields. General publishing can omit the thumbnail, with the warning **X will show a plain link card, not the playable game**; the X game workflow requires it. X decides actual inline playback, so the complete game must work in a browser too. Free accounts can keep two games live. Updates use the same slot; offer unpublish or the existing [Voyager billing flow](https://voyager.so/dashboard/billing) when the cap is reached. Free, Starter, and accounts without a plan receive a quick, permissive AI safety check that fails open on a model outage or timeout. Plans above Starter skip content checks; structural bundle validation applies to every plan. For HTTP 402 `free_game_limit`, offer unpublish or upgrade. For a rare HTTP 422 `content_flagged` refusal, show the service reason verbatim and stop without automatic retry or rewriting. Follow publish-game for user-requested fixes and ordinary upstream errors. Never remove another game or bypass a refusal automatically. Publication, update and title changes may take up to 20 seconds to appear at an edge location; unpublish stops new requests within 30 seconds. ## Layout Implement `?embed=1` on the same page, filling the square without page chrome. Keep all controls, score and restart in the frame. Test this mode and the full browser game. For Voyager, build `index.html`, the required poster, and local assets; do not add host configuration files. Only for the user's own static host: the card tags live in `index.html`. With Vite, put `poster.png`, `robots.txt` and `_headers` in `public/` so the build copies them into `dist/`. ``` dist/ index.html share page: card tags, and the full game poster.png the card's image (1:1, about 1200×1200, under 5 MB) robots.txt must not block Twitterbot _headers framing header (Cloudflare Pages, Netlify) ``` `index.html?embed=1` is the player URL. The page reads the flag to drop page chrome and show "Open full game ↗". A game with several pages carries the flag on every navigation; losing it can blank the frame on hosts that only allow embed pages to be framed. On Voyager the link targets the stable root, never the versioned `/_v/…` document it redirects to: ```html Open full game ↗ ``` On the user's own host, a shared-room game links the current room's share page, `/r/` (see "Shared rooms"), not the `/play/` player. ## Card tags on the user's own host Voyager generates these tags automatically from the publication and thumbnail; the example below is for the user's own host. On Voyager, verify the actual emitted tags after publishing. Card URLs are absolute, so build them from the deployed origin (a `SITE_URL` build variable) and never from relative paths. Escape the text. ```html ``` On the user's own host, add `twitter:site` when the user supplies a handle and version the poster URL when its bytes change. On Voyager, Studio supplies the versioned poster URL; keep sharing the stable root URL. Do not claim these tags guarantee rendering in an X client. ## Framing headers Voyager permits embedding on any site, including X. It owns these headers; verify the final player response has no restrictive `frame-ancestors` or `X-Frame-Options` header. Do not try to change Voyager hosting restrictions with a bundled `_headers` file or meta tag. For the user's own host, an equivalent unrestricted framing policy is: ``` Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors * ``` The share page must send no `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`, or `unsafe-none`: the new tab inherits X's frame sandbox, and Chromium blocks any other value with `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_RESPONSE`. Check the final response for a conflicting `X-Frame-Options: DENY` or `SAMEORIGIN`, and verify that the `embed=1` flag survives redirects and in-game navigation. Header checks establish that framing is permitted; only a real post establishes what X actually renders. For Cloudflare Pages, place it in a `_headers` file in the deployed folder: ``` /* Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors * ``` ## Cloudflare Pages alternative Use this only when the user chooses their own host. Pages is not required for Voyager publishing, and Pages alone does not provide a shared-room server. Keep credentials outside the game files. 1. Inspect the user's existing setup with `npx wrangler whoami`. If not signed in, the user runs `npx wrangler login` in their own terminal. Never create or sign in to an account for them. 2. Resolve the user's chosen account and project, and its stable production origin. Build absolute card URLs from that origin, using `/?embed=1` for the player and a square poster URL. Escape title/description text and configure the framing header above. 3. Build with relative local asset paths. When deploying to that project is authorized, use `npx wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name PROJECT --branch main`, replacing `main` with the actual production branch. Share the stable production origin, not a deployment preview. 4. Run the Twitterbot, HTTPS 200, framing and real-client checks below. If `robots.txt` exists, verify it does not block Twitterbot. Consult current provider documentation before changing deployment setup or advising on provider limits and pricing. ## Mock post Keep this beside the source, out of the deployed folder, and open it from the dev server. It exercises a square frame and common iframe restrictions. Actual X restrictions can differ; local mock success does not establish inline playback in X. ```html Post preview
``` ## Checks after publishing Use the actual returned root URL and no account credentials. Follow redirects: a root redirect is not the final player document. Wait up to the 20-second edge visibility window after publishing. ```sh GAME_URL='https://ACTUAL_GAME_HOST.voyager.site' mkdir -p .voyager/tmp curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 30 --location --max-redirs 5 --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --user-agent Twitterbot "$GAME_URL/" --output .voyager/tmp/voyager-game-card.html rg 'twitter:|og:' .voyager/tmp/voyager-game-card.html curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 30 --location --max-redirs 5 --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --user-agent Twitterbot "$GAME_URL/?embed=1" --dump-header .voyager/tmp/voyager-game-player.headers --output /dev/null --write-out 'player HTTP %{http_code}\n' rg -i 'HTTP/|content-security-policy|x-frame-options|cross-origin-opener-policy' .voyager/tmp/voyager-game-player.headers # Copy the exact absolute twitter:image value from the fetched document: POSTER_URL='https://ACTUAL_GAME_HOST.voyager.site/ACTUAL_VERSIONED_POSTER_PATH' curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 30 --location --max-redirs 5 --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --user-agent Twitterbot "$POSTER_URL" --output /dev/null --write-out 'poster HTTP %{http_code}\n' ``` Inspect the output, not just the exit codes: - `twitter:card` must be `player`; `twitter:player` must be the stable root `/?embed=1`. - The title and `twitter:image` must match the release. Width and height must both be `480`. - Both player and poster must return final HTTP `200` over HTTPS. - The final player must permit any site to frame it; a restrictive `frame-ancestors` or conflicting `X-Frame-Options` fails the check. Framing permission does not relax restrictions on what the game itself can do. - `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` must be absent or `unsafe-none`, or "Open full game ↗" fails from X. In the mock post, it must open the full game in a new tab. - Play the actual player with pointer input, at square and phone sizes, through a full round and restart. A successful upload or local preview is insufficient to claim the release is ready. If the public checks fail, report what failed and fix it. If they pass but X shows a poster or link, record the client and observed behavior. X can cache card data; do not create another publication or change the stable share URL to force a different card. Only a real post proves inline behavior. The user posts the link unless they explicitly ask for posting through an authorized account connection. ## Shared rooms Voyager's hosting is static and blocks external network connections. It cannot host shared rooms, even when their client builds successfully. Shared play needs the user's own server and hosting/security policy that allows its connections. Cloudflare Pages alone is static too; a Worker/Durable Object or another server is a separate deployment requiring user intent. Everyone who opens the post joins one live game, so the link names a room (`/r/` serving the card, with the player at `/play/`). That needs a server: for example a Cloudflare Worker with one Durable Object per room running the authoritative simulation at about 20 ticks a second over a WebSocket. - Send compact messages, and only what is near each player's view. Set `binaryType = "arraybuffer"` on the socket. - Spawn a newcomer already playing (autopilot and a brief shield), and fill quiet rooms with a few labelled bots that leave as people join. - No sign-in. Players get a guest name and can change it, kept on their device when storage allows, with a basic filter on names. - Check the host's pricing and limits with the user before deploying a server.

---
name: make-x-game
description: "Playable browser games for X posts and player cards."
---

People meet this game in a square frame inside a post, usually on a phone, and give it a few
seconds. Build for that.

Ask first, unless the request or project already answers it:

- The game in one sentence: the one mechanic, and what a tap, drag or key does.
- Solo with a high score, or shared, so everyone who opens the post plays one live room? Shared
  needs the user's own server and a host that permits those connections. Voyager hosting is
  static and blocks external network access; it cannot host shared rooms
  ([references/player-card.md](references/player-card.md), "Shared rooms").
- Hosting: Voyager can publish a built static game at a permanent `https://<slug>-<random6>.voyager.site` URL using
  the existing account. Follow [publish-game](../publish-game/SKILL.md) only when the user asks
  to publish. Use the user's own host when requested; no separate cloud login is needed for
  Voyager hosting.

For a first release, publish-game chooses a short readable game slug without brand names or
misleading affiliation; the server adds its six-character random suffix. Keep the returned URL
through every update. Renaming later changes the displayed title, not the permanent link.

Explain that Voyager supplies an X player card when the release includes its poster, while X
decides whether a client actually plays it inline. The stable share page must also be a complete
game in a browser. Give the user the game link to put in the post; a gameplay clip can go in a
separate reply. Do not promise a specific presentation in X's apps.

Build:

- One HTTPS origin serving the share page, which is itself the full game. **Implement and test
  `?embed=1`** on the same page: it fills the iframe without page chrome. Voyager's player URL
  is always the stable root plus `?embed=1`; Studio supplies the title, poster, player tags,
  480×480 dimensions and headers permitting embedding on any site, including X. Do not invent player options or dimensions
  in the upload manifest. Tags, headers, layout and a mock post are in the reference.
- A square game that fills whatever box it gets. X is told 480×480 but clients scale the frame,
  and it never scrolls: size the canvas from the viewport, and keep every control, the score and
  the restart inside it.
- Playing in the first second: no title screen or menu. Open in an attract mode (autopilot or a
  demo round) that the first input takes over. Rounds last 20 to 90 seconds and restart with one
  tap; show the score and the best.
- Pointer events first, with `touch-action: none` on the canvas and no context menu. Keys are a
  bonus, since they reach the frame only after a click, and arrows and space must never scroll.
- Sound starts muted, unlocks on the first input, and has a mute toggle.
- The frame is sandboxed: never use `<form>` (submission is blocked), `alert`, `confirm` or
  `prompt`. In embed mode a corner "Open full game ↗" link opens the share page without
  `embed=1` (on Voyager the stable root `/`; a shared room's own `/r/<room>`) with
  `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and the `embed=1` flag survives any in-game
  navigation.
- Storage may be partitioned or denied in X's frame: wrap `localStorage`, keep state in memory,
  and never fail to start because storage threw.
- Small and fast: a plain canvas or WebGL game, or Phaser or three.js when the game needs one,
  with every asset bundled on the same origin. Aim for a playable frame within two seconds on a
  phone and no mixed content.
- **Require a square PNG/JPEG/WebP poster** showing gameplay, the game title and **"Tap to play"**,
  made with make-image or captured from the game. Aim for 1200×1200 and readable text at card
  size. Include it in the built folder and pass `--thumbnail-path poster.png` to both prepare
  and publish. Do not release an X game without this poster. Voyager versions the hosted asset
  URL when publishing updates; keep sharing the stable root URL.

Follow make-web-game for the build loop (Vite with `base: './'`, the preview tools, sprites,
sound and music).

For a requested public release, follow [publish-game](../publish-game/SKILL.md) and share its
root URL. Free accounts allow two live games. Free, Starter, and accounts without a plan receive
a quick, permissive AI safety check that fails open on a model outage or timeout; plans above
Starter skip content checks. Structural bundle validation applies to every plan. Follow that
skill's limit/refusal handling.
New publication, update and title changes can take up to 20 seconds to reach an edge location.
The reference's Cloudflare Pages
steps apply only when the user chooses their own hosting. Never sign in or create an account
for them. Creating and playtesting a game alone never authorizes public publication.

Test:

- Play through real input with `preview_click` and `preview_press`, at 480×480 and at a phone
  width with `preview_resize` (`{mode: "freeform", width, height}`), and inside the mock post,
  which applies X's sandbox. Expose game state on `window` for `preview_evaluate`; look with
  `preview_snapshot`. Lose a round and restart it; do not jump to an ending.
- After publishing, follow redirects and verify that Twitterbot receives `twitter:card=player`,
  the root `/?embed=1` player URL, the actual poster URL, and width/height `480`. Require final
  HTTPS 200 responses for both player and poster, and verify the final player permits framing
  on any site without a restrictive `frame-ancestors` or `X-Frame-Options` header. Use the reference's
  terminal checks and inspect the returned values; a successful upload alone is insufficient.
- Only a real post shows whether the card plays. The user posts the link; never post for them.
  Keep the stable Voyager root URL through updates. X may cache cards, so ask what x.com and
  the phone apps showed: the game inline, only the poster, or a browser.

Finish with the link to post, the controls, what was tested where, and which clients remain
unverified. A short gameplay clip from `preview_recording_start` makes a good post or reply.
